statements.t: “In the third quarter, we delivered $314.7 million in revenue, outperforming the top end of our guidance by $12.7 million and setting a new record for the highest level of quarterly revenue in TaskUs' history," said Co-Founder and CEO Bryce Maddock.
"In light of our results, sustained sales momentum, and the continued strength of our service offerings, we are raising our full-year revenue outlook by $20 million at the midpoint.

We delivered another quarter ahead of our guidance on both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, with year-to-date Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $101.6 million, or 58% of Adjusted EBITDA," said Chief Financial Officer Rishabh Khemka.

"As a result, we are increasing our full-year 2026 revenue range to between $1.249 billion and $1.251 billion and expect to earn full-year Adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 19% at the midpoint of our revenue guidance.
Additionally, our strong year-to-date free cash flow gives us the confidence to again increase our full-year Adjusted Free Cash Flow outlook by $5 million to $120 million at the midpoint.

At the midpoint of our guidance, net cash provided by operating activities for the full year 2026 is expected to be approximately $165 million and purchase of property and equipment is expected to be approximately $45 million.

Our Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance and expected net cash provided by operating activities excludes the impact of certain payments, including transaction costs, liability stock-based compensation awards and operational efficiency costs, due to the unpredictability of the costs and timing of payments.
TaskUs senior management will host a conference call today to discuss the Company’s third quarter 2026 financial results and financial outlook.
A replay of the audio webcast will be available on the Company’s Investor Relations website for 12 months following the call.

TaskUs anticipates that it will continue to report both GAAP and certain non-GAAP financial measures in its financial results, including non-GAAP results that exclude the impact of certain costs, losses and gains that are required to be included in our profit and loss measures under GAAP.

Our management believes that the inclusion of supplementary adjustments to EBITDA applied in presenting Adjusted EBITDA are appropriate to provide additional information to investors about certain material non-cash items and about unusual items that we do not expect to continue at the same level in the future.

Our management believes that the inclusion of supplementary adjustments to earnings per share applied in presenting Adjusted EPS are appropriate to provide additional information to investors about certain material non-cash items and about unusual items that we do not expect to continue at the same level in the future.

Our management believes that the inclusion of these supplementary adjustments to Free Cash Flow are appropriate to provide additional information to investors about these unusual items that we do not expect to continue at the same level in the future.
